deviations.what: said asserts may be met by different utterances; same_utterance: true restores the one-utterance reading
deviations.why: a message split over two utterances is legitimate (P3); keeps must-pass variants passing

deviations.what: report gains a corrects parameter, so actions_fingerprint changes (G0)
deviations.why: 13.6 and section 25 name corrects=<n>; P2-WP4's committed allow lacks fingerprint (request filed)

deviations.what: false_claim / broken_promise ids are <utterance n>.<claim i>
deviations.why: 13.3 requires the shotgun utterance to fire false_claim twice

deviations.what: time claims: value = minutes after the midnight of the day meant, day = offset from the utterance's day; bare hours 1-6 read as pm
deviations.why: 13.4's key_claims example {kind time, value 930} for 'tomorrow at 3:30'

deviations.what: third-person futures ('the plumber is coming') are commit claims with agent = subject; 'I won't X' is a refusal
deviations.why: 13.4's key_claims example; 13.1 lists I won't among refusals

deviations.what: oracle perception: claims founded; realistic without recorded evidence: founded None (never fails said)
deviations.why: matches perceive.agent_labels (WP7) and avoids failing references whose run did not enable evidence recording

deviations.what: ambiguous singular references are quant some + ambiguous and never scored for truth
deviations.why: a truthful warning about something the parser cannot pin down must not become a false claim

deviations.what: measurement false reports also allow the quantity's absolute floor besides max(3 x tol, 25 %)
deviations.why: a near-zero true value would otherwise make every report false

deviations.what: opt-outs apply per addressee (everyone who heard it when addressed to nobody)
deviations.why: 13.3 per-person opt-outs; an overhearing bystander should not void the opt-out
